title: fix-rare-kv-eviction-stall-causing-long-context-tail-latency-across-deployments
creator: Maya Chen
description: Several customers (Host: SparkDocs, Private: AcmeHealth) reported intermittent severe tail latency for long-context requests. Root cause analysis shows a rare interaction between the continuous batching scheduler's priority window and aggressive KV-cache eviction that results in request starvation: long-context requests trigger large KV allocations which are evicted mid-rollout; the scheduler mistakenly deprioritizes those inflight lanes leading to prolonged queue waits. The problem manifests across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments but is most visible under mixed-priority workloads and when cache pressure is high.
acceptance_criteria: No regression in standard latency P50/P90 for existing workloads
Reproducible failure scenario fixed in canary: long-context requests no longer observe >3x tail latency spikes under simulated cache pressure
Hotfix deployed to hosted, canary to Dedicated pool, and documented private patch with upgrade notes
Added smoke tests and e2e test covering eviction+priority-window scenario
Customer confirmations from SparkDocs and AcmeHealth that escalations are resolved
steps_taken: 03-01: Triage call with on-call, SRE, and customer success; captured reproducible load pattern from SparkDocs and AcmeHealth
03-02: Reproduced locally by synthesizing mixed short+long-context traffic with tiny cache allocation limit; validated long requests got starved in scheduler logs
03-03: Added verbose tracing to scheduler path to capture request lifecycle and priority window transitions

03-04: Identified two contributing bugs: (1) eviction callback released KV tokens but scheduler kept lane marked as occupied, (2) scheduler priority aging bumped lanes out of active window when KV reallocation occurred mid-batch

03-05: Implemented hotfix branch: ensure eviction triggers immediate lane reclamation and add atomic lane state transition to prevent double-counting; adjust priority window to prefer lanes with recent KV touch
03-06: Run perf bench on a canary Dedicated pool and hosted staging; observed 70-90% reduction in P99 tail spikes for long-context synthetic workload
manual_steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start runtime with KV cache size artificially reduced (env: KV_CACHE_MAX=32MB)
2) Launch mixed traffic: 80% short requests (<=64 tokens) at 800 rps, 20% long-context requests (~8192 tokens) at 5 rps
3) Observe scheduler debug logs for lane state transitions and eviction callbacks
4) Measure tail latency; failing runs show periodic >3x P99 spikes aligned with eviction events
hotfix_release_plan: Host: apply hotfix to runtime-1.22-hosted canary and monitor for 12h before global rollout
Dedicated: rollout hotfix to one reserved pool as canary, validate throughput/lossless KPIs, then roll remaining pools over 48h
Private: prepare patch bundle and upgrade notes; coordinate with top-affected customers (AcmeHealth) for scheduled maintenance window
All: add runtime flag runtime.scheduler.eviction_atomic=true default true after validation
monitoring_and_alerting_changes: Alert: spike in scheduler.lane_stalled_count > 10/min triggers on-call
Dashboard: KV eviction events correlated with request tail latency (p50/p90/p99 overlays)
Synthetic job: nightly eviction-pressure scenario run with regression gating
next_steps: Finalize PR review and merge hotfix branch (PR #8345)
Complete canary verification window for hosted cluster and gather customer confirmations
Ship private patch bundle and post-upgrade validation script
Add unit tests for eviction -> lane reclamation path and scheduler e2e for priority aging race
Write postmortem and include guidance for tuneable KV cache defaults and scheduler flags
